answer: A stake-weighted reputation market works like a cedar forest: each agent must lock a deposit before it can vouch for others, and its endorsements pass through a prism of peer review, where every claim is checked against independent attestations, so fake identities cannot borrow credibility. Honest agents build a reef of shared history over time; a sybil swarm starts with no history and must fund each fake identity separately, pay the lockup for every one, and keep them all active, so cloning a thousand voices costs a thousand deposits while earning almost no trusted reputation.
